title: He didn’t stutter.
paragraphs: He didn’t stutter.
“Go… and make disciples.” — Matthew 28:19

Not buildings.
Not brands.
Not “my church vs your church.”
Disciples.
People who die to self and live for Christ.
But here’s where it gets uncomfortable.

We got busy multiplying stages…
while Jesus was calling us to multiply surrendered lives.

We built denominations with labels—
Baptist. Pentecostal. Reformed. Catholic.
And listen—some scholars interpret these as necessary structures for order, teaching, and accountability.
That’s true.
But structure was never meant to replace transformation.
Because you can sit in a church your whole life…
…and still not follow Jesus.
You can know the songs, the language, the culture—
…but not carry the cross.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Jesus didn’t die to make you religious.
He died to make you new.

A disciple is not someone who attends.
A disciple is someone who obeys.
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself…” — Luke 9:23
That’s the call.

Not comfort.
Not popularity.
Surrender.
So yes—plant churches.
But don’t forget why.
A true church is not a logo or a denomination.
It’s a people being shaped into the image of Jesus.
Let me ask you straight:
Are you just part of a church…
or are you actually a disciple?
Jesus is still calling.

Not to religion.
To relationship.
To repentance.
To a cross… and an empty tomb.
And there is grace for you—right now.
